setlist.title: It Must Have Been The Roses

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Playing In The Band** (2 reviews, 2 other sources): Playin' > Wharf Rat > Truckin' (small cut) > Playin' sequence praised; the Nobody's Fault jam lasts only about 15 seconds; Playin' goes interesting places yet makes more sense than usual 1974 versions, with a sweet segue into Wharf Rat [2][4][9][13]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Scarlet ends with a faded-out cut while the band is still playing hard [10]

## Setlist highlights

- Earliest performances in the archive: Playing In The Band Jam [19]

## The recordings

- **gd1974-07-21.ecm22p.bertrando.motb0056.88979.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 24 songs; 177 min; rated 4.5/5 by 12 [1]
- **gd1974-07-21.sony22p.bertrando-miller.88553.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 23 songs; 183 min; rated 4.17/5 by 12 [2]
- **gd74-07-21.fob-patched.miller.31436.sbeok.flacf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 172 min; rated 4.3/5 by 10 [4]. Said about its sound: Vocals are mostly drowned out, though the second set sounds somewhat better; reviewer wanted better microphone work [14]
- **gd74-07-21.bertrando.weiner.8241.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 171 min; rated 4.5/5 by 14 [5]. Said about its sound: Excellent audience recording for its era: little crowd noise, and the bass comes through clearly; Sound is quite listenable; Audience tape conveys the Wall of Sound sound better than soundboards can [8][9][12]

## Around the show

- Taper's surroundings include joking banter, such as a request for a roach clip; crowd quiets when jams begin [10]
- The show is not in the band's vault, so this audience recording is the only source [16]
- The second set was Phil & Ned, consisting of Seastones, with the third set beginning at China Cat Sunflower [4]
- U.S. Blues was the encore [5]
- Judged a routine 1974 show, less groundbreaking than the 6/26, 8/4 or 8/6 shows [7]
- From China Cat > Rider onward the show is wonderful, and shouldn't be overlooked among the many good 1974 shows [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1974-07-21.ecm22p.bertrando.motb0056.88979.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Rob Bertrando; transferred by Adam Egert; source: 2 x Sony ECM-22P => Sony TC-152SD >> MAC >> Sony TC-D5M => TEAC AN-300 [Dolby Encode] => Technics RS-1506US [3.75 IPS] [1]
- **gd1974-07-21.sony22p.bertrando-miller.88553.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Rob Bertrando; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Sony ECM-22P -> Cassette Master -> Reel -> Dat DAround [2]. Also: Cassette master lent by Rob Bertrando, from unknown mics, with cassette copies supplying Scarlet Begonias' ending from 6:27 [2]
- **gd74-07-21.fob-patched.miller.31436.sbeok.flacf**: taped by Rob Bertrando and Ed Friedman; transferred by Charlie Miller and Ken Stuart; source: Audience: Sony ECM-22P [4]. Also: Appears to be an entirely new transfer as well as patched, per the text file; Scarlet Begonias' ending and part of Truckin' are patched from an unknown-mic audience cassette master copy [4][15]
- **gd74-07-21.bertrando.weiner.8241.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: Sony ECM-22P mics [5]. Also: A complete-show version exists, patching this source with a previously uncirculated source via Charlie Miller; Taped with Rob Bertrando's Sony ECM-22P mics onto a Sony TC-152 cassette master, later reel, DAT and CD [5][11]

## Art and photos

- Poster by www.gratefulseconds.com: [The Wall Comes to the Hollywood Bowl, July 21, 1974](http://www.gratefulseconds.com/2017/03/the-wall-comes-to-hollywood-bowl-july.html) [20]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [current-page:url:arg:3 | Grateful Dead](https://www.dead.net/tags/hollywood-bowl) [21]
